evals.name: new-project-with-postgres-and-jwt
evals.prompt: I need to create a new Minimal API project at C:\dev\sandbox\PedidosApi. It'll use PostgreSQL as the database and JWT authentication. API documentation can just be the native .NET one, no Swagger.
evals.expected_output: A new ASP.NET Core Minimal API project created at the given path via the dotnet CLI, with EF Core + Npgsql configured, JWT bearer authentication wired in, endpoints organized into extension methods instead of inline in Program.cs, and a final dotnet build confirmed to succeed before the task is reported as done.
assertions: The skill runs a real dotnet SDK check (dotnet --version or dotnet --list-sdks) before generating anything.

The skill does not ask about database/auth/documentation choices that the user already answered in the prompt (Postgres, JWT, native docs) — it proceeds directly to generation for those, at most confirming understanding.
The generated project includes an EF Core provider package for PostgreSQL (e.g. Npgsql.EntityFrameworkCore.PostgreSQL) referenced in the .csproj.
Program.cs delegates endpoint registration to extension methods rather than defining every route inline.
The skill runs dotnet build against the generated project and reports the build result explicitly, not just that files were created.
No real client, company, or internal hostname appears anywhere in generated code, comments, or connection strings — only placeholder values.

evals.name: sdk-missing-guidance-only
evals.prompt: I want to create a new Minimal API called CatalogoApi, but I think I don't have the .NET SDK installed on this machine.
evals.expected_output: The skill checks for the .NET SDK, confirms it is missing, and asks the user whether they want setup guidance. If the user says yes, it provides OS-appropriate step-by-step installation instructions without executing any installation command itself, and does not proceed to generate the project until the user confirms the SDK is ready.
assertions: The skill explicitly runs or references a real dotnet SDK detection command before concluding it is missing.
The skill asks the user for confirmation before giving installation guidance, rather than dumping instructions unprompted.
The installation guidance is specific to an operating system rather than a single generic link, and does not include the skill running an install/configure command on the user's behalf.
The skill does not proceed to project generation (dotnet new) within this same response, since the SDK was reported missing.

evals.name: simple-project-no-database
evals.prompt: Create a simple Minimal API project called HealthCheckApi, no database, no authentication, and with Scalar for API documentation. You can generate it in the current directory.
evals.expected_output: A minimal, dependency-light ASP.NET Core Minimal API project generated via dotnet CLI with Scalar wired in for API documentation, no database or auth packages added, endpoints organized via extension methods, and a successful dotnet build confirmed at the end.
assertions: No EF Core or database provider package is added, consistent with the user's 'no database' answer.
No authentication/authorization middleware or package is added, consistent with the user's 'no auth' answer.
A Scalar package/middleware is referenced for API documentation instead of Swashbuckle or no documentation at all.
The skill runs dotnet build and reports the outcome before considering the task complete.
